scanPrep.context:
Summary: Audited BrokenCrystals (NestJS/Fastify) codebase and runtime: no NestJS ThrottlerModule, express-rate-limit, or any in-memory rate-limiter/guard exists in source; no account-lockout logic in the app; CSRF is optional (only enforced when op=csrf/csrf_dom) and is replayable via cookie value injection, so left untouched; Keycloak's bruteForceProtected is already false (confirmed both in realm-export.json and live via Keycloak admin API), and its registration-recaptcha-action authenticator is DISABLED. No server-side CAPTCHA enforcement exists anywhere reachable. Verified with 8 rapid-fire POST requests to /api/auth/login (same admin credentials) — all returned clean HTTP 201 with no 429s or throttle-related error bodies. No code or config changes were required.
Recovery guidance (security controls): If a future scan still hits 429s or captcha-like blocks, re-check: (1) Keycloak admin realm settings via `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/brokencrystals` for bruteForceProtected/failureFactor, (2) any reverse proxy added in front of the app (none present currently), (3) re-grep src/ for 'Throttler|rate-limit|express-brute' in case new deps were added, since currently none exist and none needed patching.
Recovery guidance (2FA/MFA): Investigation details for future reference: This is the BrokenCrystals app. Keycloak (keycloak/imports/realm-export.json) defines an OTP policy (otpPolicyType: totp) and a CONFIGURE_TOTP required action, but that action has \"defaultAction\": false and no user entry (including the seeded admin-cli/brokencrystals-client service accounts) lists CONFIGURE_TOTP in its \"requiredActions\" array — so TOTP is never actually required to log in. The app's own primary login flow (POST /api/auth/login with body {\"user\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"admin\",\"op\":\"basic\"}) does not call Keycloak for this path and has zero 2FA/MFA/TOTP code anywhere in src/ (grep for twoFactor|2fa|mfa|totp|otp|authenticator found nothing in app source, only Keycloak config/realm JSON and unrelated matches like 'platformFaultDomain'). Verified end-to-end: logged in as admin/admin -> HTTP 201 with an 'authorization' JWT header and no 2FA prompt; then called GET /api/users/me with that token -> HTTP 200 returning {\"firstName\":\"admin\",\"lastName\":\"admin\",\"id\":1,\"isAdmin\":true}, i.e. full access with no 401/403 and no redirect to a 2FA/onboarding step. If a future scan run somehow triggers a 2FA requirement (e.g. via the OIDC/Keycloak login path at /api/auth/admin/login or OIDC op mode), check keycloak/imports/realm-export.json's \"requiredActions\" for CONFIGURE_TOTP on specific users, or query Keycloak's user DB/API (docker exec into brokencrystals-keycloak-1 or brokencrystals-keycloak-db-1) and clear any CONFIGURE_TOTP required actions, then restart with 'docker compose -f compose.local.yml up -d --build keycloak nodejs'. For now, no source, env, or DB changes were made since none were required.
